overview.heading: What is BDS?
paragraphs: BDS, or Bachelor of Dental Surgery, is an undergraduate degree in dentistry in India that usually takes five years to complete, including four years of study and a compulsory one-year internship. It prepares students to care for teeth, gums, and other parts of the mouth through classroom learning, lab work, and supervised clinical practice.

Students who choose BDS usually need a strong foundation in Physics, Chemistry, and Biology, and admission is generally through NEET UG. The course suits people who want a healthcare career with regular patient contact and practical procedures rather than mainly desk-based study.

After BDS, graduates may work as dentists in clinics, hospitals, public health settings, or teaching roles, and some go on to MDS for further specialisation. A BDS degree is an important step toward practice, but independent work comes after the internship and the required registration or licence.

snapshot.data_note: In India, BDS pay changes with the type of workplace, city, experience, and whether a graduate works in a private clinic, hospital, teaching role, or specialist setting. New graduates are often near the lower end, while experienced dentists and those with postgraduate study can earn more, so one number cannot describe.

salary.note: Published figures for India commonly place BDS starting pay around INR 300000 to INR 320000 a year, with broader ranges extending from about INR 100000 to INR 700000 and senior or specialist roles reaching higher.

curriculum.assessment_methods: Continuous internal assessment, theory examinations, practical examinations, viva voce, clinical case presentation, logbook review, and completion of the compulsory rotatory internship.
curriculum.learning_activities: Lectures, dissection and laboratory sessions, pre-clinical and clinical simulations, chairside patient care, departmental postings, case discussions, community oral health work, seminars, and supervised internship rotations.

parent_corner.intro: BDS suits students who like biology, patient interaction, and practical work. The course is a serious professional path, so families should look beyond just admission and think about the full route: Class 12 science, entrance preparation, the five-year degree, and the steps needed before independent practice. In India, the usual entry route is through NEET UG, so academic consistency matters more than last-minute cramming. After graduation, a student cannot simply open a clinic without completing the required registration process. Parents can help by checking whether the child enjoys clinical settings, can handle long hours of focused study, and is willing to work with hygiene, responsibility, and communication. It also helps to compare private and government colleges carefully, because fees can vary widely.
